answer: Sybil resistance holds when an identity costs something that does not scale with how many you mint. One mechanism: every agent must burn a verifiable proof-of-work whose difficulty equals roughly an hour of compute. Trivial for a real newcomer, prohibitive for someone spawning ten thousand. Call it a bridge toll paid in copper, not promises: each crossing costs actual metal, and a bot farm cannot print metal by demanding more crossings. Add a spiral of rising per-origin fees, and mass registration collapses on itself. Honest agents pay once; forgers drown in arithmetic.
